extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of poetry, literary criticism, and philosophy (readers interested in imagination, memory, and theory of perception)
extracted.subtask_description: Expository treatment of the faculties (imagination, memory, will) as they pertain to poetry and philosophy, and critical standards for acceptable philosophical systems and poetic practice. Useful for writers and critics considering what makes poetic imagination, memory, and philosophical explanation adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination as an intermediate active-and-passive faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: There are evidently two powers at work, which relatively to each other are active and passive; and this is not possible without an intermediate faculty, which is at once both active and passive. In philosophical language, we must denominate this intermediate faculty in all its degrees and determinations, the IMAGINATION.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the subject of poetry, the term 'imagination' is appropriated to a superior degree of the faculty, joined to a superior voluntary control over it. The imagination mediates between passive sensations and voluntary acts of thought; it both receives and exerts influence, and so must be cultivated for poetic production (i.e. voluntary control over imaginative play is a mark of poetic power).

rubrics_metrics.name: Will/attention as a means of producing vividness (Arts of Memory)
rubrics_metrics.description: The will itself by confining and intensifying the attention may arbitrarily give vividness or distinctness to any object whatsoever; and from hence we may deduce the uselessness, if not the absurdity, of certain recent schemes which promise an artificial memory...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, memory and recollection depend less on mechanical mnemonic schemes and more on disciplined attention; the 'Arts of Memory' consist in habits and conditions that render impressions vivid: sound logic, philosophical knowledge of facts in causal relation, a cheerful and communicative temper, a quiet conscience, sound health, and (for passive remembrance) a healthy digestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of the genuine 'Arts of Memory'
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound logic, as the habitual subordination of the individual to the species, and of the species to the genus; philosophical knowledge of facts under the relation of cause and effect; a cheerful and communicative temper; a quiet conscience; a condition free from anxieties; sound health, and above all (as far as relates to passive remembrance) a healthy digestion; these are the best, these are the only Arts of Memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and poets should cultivate intellectual habits, moral calm, temperamental cheerfulness, and bodily health rather than rely on artificial mnemonic tricks. The passage explicitly dismisses artificial memory schemes as producing confusion and debasement of the fancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish conditions from causes (avoid paralogism)
rubrics_metrics.description: The common sophism is the mistaking the conditions of a thing for its causes and essence; and the process, by which we arrive at the knowledge of a faculty, for the faculty itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing mental faculties or artistic processes, do not conflate what makes an experience possible (condition) with what constitutes its essence (cause). Example: 'The air I breathe is the condition of my life, not its cause.' This is recommended as a methodological safeguard when critiquing theories (e.g., Hartley's scheme).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneity/continuity as condition of association, not its essence
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporaneity, then, being the common condition of all the laws of association, and a component element in the materia subjecta, the parts of which are to be associated, must needs be co-present with all. Nothing, therefore, can be more easy than to pass off on an incautious mind this constant companion of each, for the essential substance of all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In creative work and psychology, remember that mere simultaneity or proximity (time/space continuity) explains some associations, but likeness and contrast also operate; the true determinant is what makes parts of an impression more vivid or distinct. Authors should attend to what creates vividness rather than attribute associative effects solely to contemporaneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: A successful theory of perception must explain formation of the associable
rubrics_metrics.description: All association demands and presupposes the existence of the thoughts and images to be associated... the hypothesis neither involves the explanation, nor precludes the necessity, of a mechanism and co-adequate forces in the percipient, which at the more than magic touch of the impulse from without is to create anew for itself the correspondent object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For theories (or poetic metaphors) that claim perceptions derive from external stimuli, one must still explain how the percipient's mechanism produces the immediate presence of the object; the mere pre-existence of an original image/external world is insufficient. In artistic terms: depiction/copy requires repetition of the creative process, not just reference to an original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion of intelligibility and explanatory power for philosophical systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The hypothesis of Hylozoism... is the death of all rational physiology... But it is not either the nature of man, or the duty of the philosopher to despair concerning any important problem until... How the esse assumed as originally distinct from the scire, can ever unite itself with it; how being can transform itself into a knowing, becomes conceivable on one only condition; namely, if it can be shown that the vis representativa, or the Sentient, is itself a species of being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable philosophical (or theoretical) systems must be intelligible and provide a plausible account of how mind and being interrelate. Systems that multiply occult qualities or fail to explain the transition from external impact to inner perception are judged inadequate (e.g., simple materialism or hylozoism are criticized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Materialism must account for the inward (cannot explain perception by motion alone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let any reflecting mind make the experiment of explaining to itself the evidence of our sensuous intuitions, from the hypothesis that in any given perception there is a something which has been communicated to it by an impact, or an impression ab extra... Matter has no Inward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage argues that to explain thinking as a material phenomenon requires refining 'matter' into some modification of intelligence; otherwise materialism collapses. For creative theorizing, don't reduce mental life to mere motion without positing an inward explanatory principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of heartfelt simplicity over polished orthography
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be easy to discover any substantial ground for this contemptuous pride in those literati... unless it be, that they could write orthographically, make smooth periods, and had the fashions of authorship almost literally at their fingers’ ends, while the latter, in simplicity of soul, made their words immediate echoes of their feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating literary work, give weight to fullness of feeling and intellectual substance ('fulness of heart and intellect') and to immediacy of expression rather than mere polished style or conventional fluency. The passage praises mystic simplicity and authenticity as often superior to learned polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline and moral character precede better philosophic receptivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Such men need discipline, not argument; they must be made better men, before they can become wiser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging with interlocutors whose errors stem from temperament or moral failings, moral improvement or discipline may be a prerequisite for intellectual progress; rhetoric alone may be insufficient. This can guide pedagogical or editorial choices: address character and habits as well as reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for philosophy as possible science (postulates required)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term, Philosophy, defines itself as an affectionate seeking after the truth; but Truth is the correlative of Being. This again is no way conceivable, but by assuming as a postulate, that both are ab initio, identical and coinherent; that intelligence and being are reciprocally each other’s substrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A philosophical system aiming to be a science must adopt certain metaphysical postulates (e.g., intelligence and being as coinherent); purely empirical starts (nihil in intellectu quod non prius in sensu) will, the text argues, undermine the logical categories and make philosophy impossible. For writers/theorists: be explicit about foundational assumptions and avoid naive empiricism when building a systematic account.
